title: Proportion of Outsourced Workers in Healthcare Institutions
what_it_is: Proportion of Outsourced Workers in Healthcare Institutions

sections.label: Outsourced public healthcare staff numbers
sections.summary: About 10,000 staff, or 13%, in public healthcare institutions are hired by third party contractors, including housekeeping, security, landscaping, pest control and food services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: About 10,000 staff, or about 13%, working in public healthcare institutions are hired by third party contractors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Some examples of outsourced workers include housekeeping staff, security guards, and staff doing landscaping, pest control and kitchen or food services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Of these outsourced staff, almost 70% of them are in roles which require them to be at the frontline or patient care areas, but less than 5% are involved in handling patient samples.

sections.label: Welfare measures for outsourced staff
sections.summary: Public healthcare institutions extended initiatives to outsourced staff, including infection control training, full PPE in high-risk areas, and inclusion in COVID-19 vaccination exercises.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, to ensure that the welfare of outsourced staff is taken care of during the COVID-19 outbreak, the public healthcare institutions have extended various initiatives to them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Outsourced staff who work in high-risk areas are trained in infection control measures and provided with full PPE, or Personal Protective Equipment, when discharging their duties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: They are also included in the COVID-19 vaccination exercises for our healthcare workers.

sections.label: Bonus for outsourced cleaners question
sections.summary: A Member cites the Budget 2020 bonus for frontline public officers and asks whether it will be extended to outsourced cleaners on the COVID-19 frontline.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As preamble, I just want to make reference to the Budget 2020 Round-up Speech delivered last year by the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance, and I quote from paragraph B24(a), "The Government will award public officers on the frontline who are directly battling with the COVID-19 disease up to one additional month of special bonus.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This will include many healthcare officers in MOH and the restructured hospitals." Sir, in the context of this, I can share that my Clementi residents tell me, and my brothers and sisters in the Labour Movement tell me, that there are cleaners serving in our hospitals, cleaners who are cleaning COVID-19 patient rooms, cleaners who are cleaning COVID-19 patient room toilets, who unfortunately, at the moment, do not qualify for this bonus because they are outsourced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, can I ask the Senior Minister of State will the Ministry consider extending this bonus to outsourced cleaners and rank and file workers who are embedded deep in the COVID-19 frontline?
